I farm 10.1 mu under a wheat-maize rotation, and I have well irrigation, so I will keep the full land in the same double-cropping system this year. I have been farming a long time, so I do not want to take risks with unstable varieties or overly aggressive input use. I will use improved seed for wheat because it is reliable and fits my usual management, and hybrid seed for maize because maize responds well to stronger seed performance. Since my household has some off-farm labor, I will keep the plan simple and practical: moderate fertilizer, a manageable number of irrigations, and standard pest control instead of pushing for maximum yield at high cost. For wheat, I will put more emphasis on nitrogen and two irrigations because stable tillering and grain filling matter on my land. For maize, I will also feed it well but keep irrigation to two times with the well, because that is enough for my conditions if the season is normal. I will use rotary tillage because it is efficient for my scale and matches a wheat-maize system well. My goal is stable output, controlled cost, and low management risk across both crops.
